analysis.title: Macro at a Glance: Latest views and forecasts
key_insights: No changes to GS forecasts flagged this week.
Global real GDP growth is expected to slow to 2.7% yoy in 2026. Higher energy prices largely offset fiscal easing and the AI boom impulse.
Global core inflation is expected to end 2026 at 2.9%, with shelter and wage inflation normalizing and energy price passthrough adding to it.
US real GDP is expected to grow 2.4% Q4/Q4 in 2026, mostly from the AI boom, whose impact is expected to decline over the next year.
US core PCE is expected to fall to 3.0% yoy in December 2026 as tariff, energy passthrough and AI demand effects fade, and to move closer to 2% in 2027.
GS expects the US unemployment rate to end 2026 at 4.2%.
GS expects one more 25bp Fed hike in December to a peak range of 4.00-4.25%, and says higher inflation could prompt another hike in March 2027.
Euro area real GDP is expected to grow 1.0% Q4/Q4 in 2026, held back by elevated energy prices and subdued consumer confidence, with growth improving next year.
Euro area core inflation is expected to peak at 2.7% yoy in 1Q27 on energy passthrough, then decline gradually to 2.0% by end-2028.
GS expects one more 25bp ECB hike in December to a peak policy rate of 2.75%.
China real GDP is expected to grow 4.6% yoy in 2026, with broad-based export strength offset by weak domestic demand. CPI/PPI are expected at 0.8%/2.8% yoy, driven by commodity price passthrough.
GS flags the Middle East conflict as the key watch item, specifically the region's energy exports and demand for its energy from consumers like China.
Market forecasts in the table: Brent at $114/bbl last vs GS $95 for 4Q26 and $87 for 1Q27, and gold at $4,057/oz last vs GS $4,605 for 4Q26 and $4,765 for 1Q27.
GS US 10-year yield forecast is 4.75% for end-2026 and 4.40% for end-2027, against 4.99% last.
earnings_insights: S&P 500 EPS: GS $375 for 2026 vs consensus $367, and GS $415 for 2027 vs consensus $426. EPS growth: GS 36% in 2026 and 11% in 2027, consensus 34% and 16%.
